title: Gangtok in 3 days: a first-timer's plan
meta_description: A 3-day Gangtok plan for first-timers: arrival and MG Marg, a Tsomgo and Baba Mandir day, dawn viewpoints, Rumtek and the monasteries, with times and costs.
summary: Three days in Gangtok works best as one easy arrival day, one permit day to Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir (with Nathu La on Wednesday to Sunday for Indians), and one day for dawn viewpoints, Enchey, the Do Drul Chorten and Rumtek. Keep the high-altitude day second, not first, and leave a buffer for permit holds.

sections.heading: The shape of a good first visit
paras: Most first-timers try to fit everything into Gangtok, and most come home tired. The town sits at about 1,650 m on a ridge, Tsomgo Lake is at 3,753 m and Nathu La at 4,310 m, and the roads between them are slow mountain roads. Our rule for a first visit is simple: arrive and rest, go high once, then spend a day on the town's monasteries and viewpoints. That order lets your body get used to 1,650 m before the climb to the lake, and it puts your flexible day last, which is useful if snow or a landslide moves the permit day.

This plan assumes three nights in Gangtok, arriving from NJP or Bagdogra on day 1 and leaving on the morning of day 4. If you have a fourth night, add Ranka and Lingdum or a slow day at Rumtek. If you are going on to Lachung or Pelling, this plan sits at the front of the trip.

sections.heading: Day 1: arrive slowly and walk MG Marg
paras: The drive up NH10 from NJP or Bagdogra is about 115–125 km and takes 4–5.5 hours through Sevoke, the Teesta valley and the Rangpo check post, where Sikkim begins. Foreign nationals show their Restricted Area Permit here; since 12 January 2026 it is applied for online on the e-FRRO portal after arriving in India. In the monsoon NH10 closes after landslides, and the detour via Kalimpong and Lava adds two to four hours. Check current road status before you travel.

Check in, drink water, and keep the first afternoon light. In the evening walk MG Marg, the pedestrian main street with benches, cafés and the town's evening crowd. Cars cannot drive on it, so they drop you at either end. Lal Market is a few minutes downhill and is best on a morning visit. Your first hotel collects the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee at check-in, valid 30 days.

sections.heading: Day 2: Tsomgo Lake, Baba Mandir and Nathu La
paras: This is a permit day, and the permit is arranged by a registered agent the day before. Hand over a photo ID and two passport-size photos on day 1. Tsomgo and Baba Mandir are open to Indians and to foreigners in groups of two or more through an agent; Nathu La is for Indian nationals only, usually open Wednesday to Sunday and closed Monday and Tuesday, and it closes after snow. Check current status before you travel.

Leave Gangtok by 7:30–8:00 am. The road climbs about 38–40 km and 1.5–2 hours to Tsomgo, passing the check post at 15th Mile and the Kyongnosla Alpine Sanctuary. The lake, whose Sikkimese name is usually explained as 'head of the lake', from tso (lake) and mgo (head), is about 836 m long and freezes in winter. From the lake the road continues to Baba Mandir, the shrine to Sepoy Harbhajan Singh, an Indian Army soldier who died near Nathu La on 4 October 1968; the temple most visitors see was built in 1982 at about 4,000 m. Nathu La, the 4,310 m pass on the border with Tibet, is another short climb when it is open.

Most vehicles turn back by early afternoon and reach Gangtok by 4 pm. A reserved vehicle for Tsomgo and Baba Mandir costs about ₹4,500–5,500 in 2026, and about ₹6,500–7,500 with Nathu La. Wear warm layers even in May, walk slowly at the lake, and skip Nathu La if anyone has a headache that does not ease.

sections.heading: Day 3: viewpoints, monasteries and Rumtek
paras: Kanchenjunga shows from Gangtok mainly on clear mornings between October and April, and it is usually gone behind cloud by 9 am. Leave at 5:00–5:30 am for Tashi View Point, about 8 km north of town on the North Sikkim road, or Ganesh Tok, a small shrine on a ridge above the town near the Himalayan Zoological Park. Hanuman Tok, a temple looked after by the Indian Army, is higher and quieter but further out. Pick one: you will not see the range better from three.

After breakfast, visit Enchey Monastery, about 3 km from the market, a Nyingma monastery built in 1909 on a site associated with the tantric master Lama Druptob Karpo. Then drive to the Do Drul Chorten, a stupa built in 1945–46 by Trulshik Rinpoche with 108 prayer wheels around it, and the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology next door, whose foundation stone was laid by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1957. Check the institute's opening days locally.

In the afternoon drive about 24 km to Rumtek, the Dharma Chakra Centre, seat of the 16th Karmapa after he left Tibet in 1959 and inaugurated in 1966. Carry a photo ID: there is a security check at the gate. You are back in town for a last evening at Lal Market and MG Marg.

sections.heading: Day 4 and what to do if the plan slips
paras: Leave by 7:00–8:00 am for an afternoon flight from Bagdogra or a train from NJP. Allow at least 5 hours for the drive, more in the monsoon. If your flight is before 1 pm, stay the last night in Siliguri instead, or move the flight.

Permits for Tsomgo and Nathu La are sometimes held for snow, especially from December to March, and occasionally for road work. If day 2 is cancelled, swap it with day 3 and go to Tsomgo on day 3. This is why we never put the permit day on the last full day. In the monsoon, keep the same order but expect cloud at the lake and a slower drive.
list: Carry two passport photos and a photo ID per person for permits
Indians: carry the same ID you gave for the permit; Nathu La checks names
Give your ID and photos to the agent by the afternoon before the permit day
Pack a warm jacket, cap and gloves for Tsomgo even in summer
Keep 2,000–3,000 rupees in cash for stalls at the lake and small entry fees

sections.heading: What these three days cost
paras: Where you sleep shapes this plan more than any sight does. Stay within a 10-minute walk of MG Marg, on Tibet Road, PS Road or the lanes behind the main street, so that your evenings need no taxi and the Tsomgo vehicle can pick you up at 7:30 am without a long climb with bags. Families with grandparents should ask how many steps lead from the road to reception, because many Gangtok hotels sit below the road with no lift. Couples who want quiet can stay on the Rumtek road or at Pangthang, but every trip into town then becomes a 20–40 minute drive, which eats into day 3.

On a budget, with shared transport, a ₹1,500–2,500 room and a shared Tsomgo seat, three nights cost about ₹7,000–10,000 per person, twin sharing, in 2026. With a private small car for all three days and a good 3-star hotel near MG Marg, expect about ₹14,000–19,000 per person. Our Gangtok weekend journeys price each version openly, including the planning fee, so you can compare like with like before you book with anyone. All figures are indicative; check current rates before you travel.

faqs.a: Yes, for a first visit. Three nights give you an arrival day, one permit day to Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir (and Nathu La for Indians on its open days) and one day for viewpoints, monasteries and Rumtek. Add a fourth night if you want Ranka and Lingdum, a slow morning at Rumtek or a buffer against snow closures in winter.

faqs.q: Which day should I go to Tsomgo Lake?
faqs.a: Go on your second day, not your first or last. A night at Gangtok's 1,650 m helps before the climb to 3,753 m, and keeping a free day afterwards means a permit held for snow or road work can be moved. Hand your ID and photos to the agent on arrival day. Check current permit status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which days is Nathu La open?
faqs.a: Nathu La is usually open to Indian tourists from Wednesday to Sunday and closed on Monday and Tuesday, and it closes after heavy snow. Some sources list fewer days, so plan for Wednesday to Sunday and confirm with your agent. Foreign nationals, including OCI cardholders as we understand it, are not allowed. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where can I see Kanchenjunga from Gangtok?
faqs.a: Tashi View Point, about 8 km north of town, Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok all face the Kanchenjunga range. Go at dawn, between 5:00 and 6:30 am, on a clear day from October to April. By mid-morning cloud usually covers the peaks, and from June to September you may not see them at all.

Mostly. Foreign nationals need a Restricted Area Permit, applied for online through e-FRRO since 12 January 2026, and can visit Tsomgo Lake in a group of two or more through a registered agent on a one-day pass. They cannot go to Nathu La. The monasteries, viewpoints and Rumtek need no extra permit. Check current rules before you travel.

faqs.q: Do I need a car for all three days?
faqs.a: No. Day 1 is a transfer and an evening walk. Day 2 needs a registered vehicle for Tsomgo, which can be a shared seat. Day 3 is easiest with a reserved car for the dawn viewpoint and Rumtek, about ₹3,500–4,500 for a full day in 2026, but much of the town can be walked.

faqs.q: Is Tsomgo Lake safe for older travellers?
faqs.a: Usually, for healthy travellers who go slowly. The lake is at 3,753 m, so walk gently, avoid the yak rides if you are unsteady and keep the visit to about an hour. People with heart or lung conditions should ask their doctor first, and anyone with a worsening headache, breathlessness or confusion should go down at once.

faqs.q: What should I wear for the Tsomgo day?
faqs.a: Layers, even in summer. Temperatures at the lake are often near freezing in the morning from November to April and cool even in May. Wear a warm jacket, cap, gloves and shoes with grip; snow boots can be rented near the check post in winter. Sunglasses and sunscreen matter, because UV is strong at 3,700 m and above.

faqs.q: Should I stay the last night in Gangtok or Siliguri?
faqs.a: Stay in Gangtok if your flight from Bagdogra or train from NJP leaves after about 1 pm, and leave by 7–8 am. For earlier departures, or in the monsoon when NH10 can close after landslides, move to Siliguri the evening before. The drive down takes 4–5.5 hours in good conditions.
